question: What is a key difference between an `interface` and a `type` alias in TypeScript?
options: They are completely different and never interchangeable
Both can describe object shapes; interfaces can be re-opened/merged (declaration merging), while `type` can also express unions, tuples, and primitives

explanation.uz: Ikkalasi ham obyekt shaklini tavsiflaydi va ko'p holatda o'zaro almashinuvchan. Farqlar: `interface` qayta ochilib birlashishi mumkin (declaration merging) va odatda obyekt/klasslar uchun; `type` esa union, tuple, primitiv va murakkab tiplarni ham ifodalaydi.
explanation.en: Both can describe object shapes and are often interchangeable. Differences: an `interface` can be re-opened and merged (declaration merging) and suits objects/classes; a `type` alias can also express unions, tuples, primitives, and more complex types.

question: What is the difference between `any` and `unknown`?
options: `any` disables type checking entirely; `unknown` is type-safe — you must narrow it (check the type) before using it

explanation.uz: `any` — tip tekshiruvini butunlay o'chiradi (xavfli). `unknown` — xavfsiz muqobil: qiymatni ishlatishdan oldin uning tipini tekshirish (narrowing) shart, aks holda kompilyator ruxsat bermaydi.
explanation.en: `any` turns off type checking entirely (unsafe). `unknown` is the type-safe alternative: you must narrow (check the type) before using the value, otherwise the compiler won't allow it.

options: It is not allowed at all

explanation.uz: `string | number` — union tip. `.toUpperCase()` faqat stringda bor, shuning uchun avval NARROWING kerak: `if (typeof x === 'string') { ... }`. Shundan so'ng TS x ni string deb biladi va metodga ruxsat beradi.
explanation.en: `string | number` is a union type. `.toUpperCase()` exists only on string, so you must NARROW first: `if (typeof x === 'string') { ... }`. Then TS knows x is a string and allows the method.

options: Reusable, type-safe code — the type T is inferred/passed so identity(5) returns number, identity('a') returns string

explanation.uz: Generiklar (`<T>`) tipni parametr sifatida oladi — qayta ishlatiladigan, tip-xavfsiz kod yaratadi. identity(5) → number, identity('a') → string qaytaradi. `any`dan farqli, tip ma'lumoti saqlanadi.
explanation.en: Generics (`<T>`) take the type as a parameter — producing reusable, type-safe code. identity(5) returns number, identity('a') returns string. Unlike `any`, the type information is preserved.

question: At RUNTIME, are TypeScript types available (e.g. can you check `if (x is MyType)`)?
options: No — types are erased during compilation to JavaScript; they exist only at compile time

explanation.uz: TypeScript tiplari faqat KOMPILYATSIYA vaqtida mavjud — tsc JS'ga o'girganda tiplar O'CHIRILADI (type erasure). Ish vaqtida (runtime) tip tekshiruvi uchun oddiy JS usullari (typeof, instanceof, xossa tekshirish) ishlatiladi.
explanation.en: TypeScript types exist only at COMPILE time — when tsc compiles to JS, types are ERASED (type erasure). At runtime you must use plain JS checks (typeof, instanceof, property checks) for type guards.

options: id is optional; name cannot change
id cannot be reassigned after creation; name is optional (may be omitted)

explanation.uz: `readonly id` — id yaratilgandan keyin o'zgartirilmaydi (faqat o'qish). `name?` — ixtiyoriy xossa, berilmasligi mumkin (type string | undefined). Ular tuzilmani aniqroq va xavfsizroq qiladi.
explanation.en: `readonly id` — id can't be reassigned after creation (read-only). `name?` — an optional property that may be omitted (type string | undefined). They make the shape more precise and safer.

question: What is the `never` type used for?
options: A value that can be anything
A value that NEVER occurs — e.g. a function that always throws or an exhaustiveness check in a switch

explanation.uz: `never` — hech qachon yuz bermaydigan qiymat tipi: masalan doim xato tashlaydigan funksiya yoki cheksiz sikl. Shuningdek switch/union'da to'liqlik (exhaustiveness) tekshiruvida ishlatiladi — barcha holatlar qamralganini kompilyator kafolatlaydi. `void` esa 'qiymat qaytarmaydi' degani.
explanation.en: `never` is the type of a value that NEVER occurs: e.g. a function that always throws or an infinite loop. It's also used for exhaustiveness checks in a switch/union — the compiler guarantees all cases are handled. `void` instead means 'returns no value'.

question:
What does this tuple type enforce?

```ts
let pair: [string, number] = ['age', 30];
```
options: A fixed-length array with specific types per position: index 0 is string, index 1 is number
An object with keys string and number

explanation.uz: Tuple — belgilangan uzunlik va har pozitsiyada aniq tipga ega massiv. `[string, number]` — 0-element string, 1-element number bo'lishi shart. ['age', 30] to'g'ri; [30, 'age'] xato bo'lardi.
explanation.en: A tuple is a fixed-length array with a specific type per position. `[string, number]` requires index 0 to be a string and index 1 a number. ['age', 30] is valid; [30, 'age'] would be an error.
